beliefs.practice: Read the Mongo connection string only from an environment variable (e.g. DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never write the actual secret into source, logs, repo files or seed fixtures. Provide a .env.example with a placeholder value.

Always connect with TLS enabled and verify server certificate (tls=true or useUnifiedTopology + tls). In Mongoose/MongoClient options set tls: true, tlsAllowInvalidCertificates: false and prefer the system CA bundle.

Reuse a single shared database connection / Mongoose connection across the Node app instead of creating one per request; configure maxPoolSize (e.g. maxPoolSize: 50) and minPoolSize to control pooling.

Choose partition key = /patientId for prescriptions and refillRequests so reads/creates for a patient are co-located; ensure all queries include patientId to avoid cross-partition fan-out and RU spikes.
Create compound indexes to support common queries: e.g. { patientId: 1, medicationName: 1 } and { patientId:1, nextRefillDate:1 } so agent lookups and eligibility checks are covered without COLLSCAN.
Add a TTL index for short-lived agent memory documents (e.g. createdAt ascending with expireAfterSeconds: 2592000 for 30 days) to avoid unbounded growth of memory collection.

When storing vector embeddings, store them as a dedicated array field (e.g. embedding: [float,...]) and create a vector index (HNSW/DiskANN) specifying the correct dimensionality and metric (cosine or euclidean). Tune HNSW params (M and efConstruction) and client ef for search (efSearch) for your latency/accuracy tradeoff.
Limit returned fields with projection (select only medication name, daysSupply, fillsRemaining, lastFillDate) rather than returning full documents in agent lookups to reduce RU and network payload.

For eligibility checks, index fields used in filters or sorts (e.g. lastFillDate, fillsRemaining) and run explain() during development to ensure queries use those indexes; revise indexes based on explain plans.

Implement retry with exponential backoff and jitter for transient errors and rate-limited responses. Specifically handle 429/TooManyRequests by honoring Retry-After and scaling back retries; limit total retry time.

Keep operations that must be atomic within a single partition key so you can use a single-partition transaction if needed; otherwise implement application-level optimistic concurrency (version field) to avoid lost updates.

Do not index very high-cardinality or frequently-updated fields (e.g. lastSeenTimestamp) unless needed; index selection increases write cost—measure RU impact and only add indexes which materially speed queries.

Provision throughput appropriately: use autoscale or set RU/s based on measured load; for development use low RU but for production anticipate spikes from agent lookups and searches. Consider database-level shared throughput for many small collections.
Use least-privilege credentials: create a database user for the app with only the needed roles/privileges (read/write on sample_healthcare_15) rather than admin keys; rotate credentials regularly.

Restrict network access to the cluster using firewall rules, VNet, or private endpoint so only the developer machine / app servers can reach the cluster; do not leave DB publicly accessible without restrictions.
Log slow queries and use explain() during development and after deploy; add or adjust indexes based on slow operations. Include RU cost in diagnostics to spot heavy queries.

Store minimal PHI in agent memory: avoid storing full patient identifiers or medication details in plain text memory documents. If PHI must be stored, use field-level encryption or rely on service-side CMEK and ensure HIPAA controls are in place.
Seed scripts must be idempotent: use upsert or create-if-not-exists semantics for collections, indexes and sample documents so the seed can be re-run safely against sample_healthcare_15.

When creating refillRequest documents, write them to the same partition (patientId) as the prescription to enable inexpensive joins/queries and, if required, multi-document transactions within the same partition.

Use explain() and the documentdb MCP server tools to verify index presence and query plan for your critical queries (prescription lookup, eligibility check, vector search) as part of automated or manual verification.
